hook_line: The dark side of the Moon is not dark, and nobody saw it until 1959.
intro: The dark side of the Moon is not dark, and nobody saw it until 1959.
facts: The Moon spins exactly once for every trip around Earth, so the same face always points at us, and no human had ever seen the far side until a Soviet probe photographed it in 1959.
It is called the dark side, but it gets just as much sunlight as the side we see, it only looks different because its crust is thicker and it has almost none of the dark lava plains.
It is also home to the South Pole Aitken basin, a crater about 2,500 kilometers across, one of the biggest impact scars anywhere in the solar system.
No spacecraft landed there until China's Chang'e 4 touched down in 2019, and it needed a relay satellite parked beyond the Moon just to send its pictures home.
title_en: The Dark Side of the Moon Isn't Dark. Here's What's Really There.
